title: Sourdough Hamburger Buns
cScaleSummary: C2 because the dough uses 1 large egg and the topping uses 1 large egg for egg wash. Across 8 buns, the cholesterol contribution is approximately 46 mg per bun.
ldlActiveSummary: LDL-Active is false because this is primarily an enriched bread built around flour, sourdough starter, water, egg, olive oil, and honey. It is not specifically structured around enough LDL-lowering ingredients to qualify as LDL Active.
intro: The hamburger bun is one of the defining breads of American cooking. Unlike crusty artisan loaves, a good burger bun is designed to be soft, compressible, and sturdy enough to hold juicy fillings without falling apart. This naturally leavened version develops flavor through traditional sourdough fermentation while maintaining the tender crumb expected from a classic burger bun.

stepGroups.title: Mix the Dough
items: Combine the 100 g active sourdough starter, 220 g warm water, 1 large egg, 35 g olive oil, and 20 g honey in a large mixing bowl.
Add the 500 g bread flour and 10 g fine salt. Mix until no dry flour remains.
Cover the dough and rest for 20 minutes.

stepGroups.title: Knead and Bulk Ferment
items: Knead the dough for 8 to 10 minutes by hand, or 5 to 6 minutes in a stand mixer, until smooth, elastic, and slightly tacky.
Transfer the dough to a lightly oiled bowl and cover.
Ferment the dough until it has expanded by approximately 50 to 75 percent and feels noticeably lighter. At 75 °F to 80 °F this typically requires 3 to 5 hours.
After the first hour of fermentation, perform one stretch-and-fold by gently pulling each side of the dough over itself.

stepGroups.title: Shape the Buns
items: Divide the dough into 8 equal portions, approximately 115 g each.
Shape each portion into a tight ball.
Flatten each ball slightly into a bun approximately 3 1/2 to 4 inches in diameter.
Arrange the shaped buns on a parchment-lined baking sheet with space between each bun.

stepGroups.title: Proof and Bake
items: Cover and proof until puffy and slightly jiggly. Depending on temperature and starter activity, this generally requires 1 1/2 to 3 hours.
Preheat the oven to 375 °F.
Beat the 1 large egg with 1 tablespoon water.
Brush the tops of the buns with the egg wash.
Sprinkle the buns with the 10 g sesame seeds.
Bake at 375 °F for 18 to 22 minutes until deep golden brown and the internal temperature reaches 195 °F to 200 °F.

stepGroups.title: Cool and Serve
items: Transfer the buns to a cooling rack.
Loosely cover the buns with a clean kitchen towel while cooling for the softest crust.
Cool for at least 20 minutes before slicing.
